answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging a staking deposit that grows with each new identity. Honest agents pay once, while a fake swarm must burn that stake for every duplicate, so forgery becomes prohibitively expensive. The network broadcasts a shared beacon stating the current deposit rate, and every node keeps a mirror of the identity registry, letting anyone audit who paid. This turns the attacker's ocean of cheap copies into an ocean of losses, making mass identity creation financially irrational.
